states.stable: Supported by maintained tests for the stated surface.
states.partial: Implemented for a documented subset; unsupported cases fail rather than silently falling back.
states.experimental: An artifact or prototype exists, but compatibility and operational guarantees are not yet complete.
states.unsupported: No supported implementation exists for this surface.

features.label: Core syntax, bindings, functions, loops, and control flow
features.notes: Interpreter, VM, and supported native C paths preserve ordered `emit` statements throughout synchronous blocks and functions, including deterministic `var` assignment barriers. Native C covers tested scalar control flow, loops, direct/closure calls, mutable-local replacement, and cleanup edges; concurrent task bodies reject `emit`, and unsupported IR is rejected during compilation. The machine-checked backend inventory records each public construct and standard-library member rather than treating partial module support as module-wide parity.

features.label: LSP synchronous control flow and lexical bindings
features.notes: The LSP analyzer has stable source-backed identity for synchronous function declarations and parameters, const/let/var bindings, assignments, while and for loop bindings, defer bodies, return expressions, break/continue statements, block expressions, and calls. Definitions and references retain exact source spans; framed definition requests prove deterministic UTF-16 locations, malformed JSON-RPC rejection, stale-version rejection, and cancellation without publishing partial results. Concurrent task bodies and asynchronous I/O remain in the broader partial row.

features.label: LSP document read and write highlights
features.notes: The LSP document-highlight method resolves the shared analyzer symbol identity and returns source-backed definition, assignment, and read occurrences with exact read/write kinds. The bounded row covers deterministic ordering, duplicate removal, astral UTF-16 ranges, malformed/out-of-document/surrogate-splitting validation, stale versions, concurrent requests, pre- and mid-request cancellation, and transactional no-partial-result behavior.

features.label: LSP source declaration navigation
features.notes: The LSP declaration method resolves the same source-backed symbol identity as definition navigation and returns the exact declaration range. The bounded row covers framed deterministic output, astral UTF-16 ranges, missing/stale/negative/out-of-document/surrogate-splitting validation, pre-cancelled requests, and identity equality with direct definition results.

features.label: LSP implementation navigation
features.notes: The LSP implementation method resolves trait-method and concrete implementation identities and returns deterministic source locations. Concrete implementation methods are indexed as method definitions and are selected when the cursor targets a trait or implementation method; duplicate URI/source-span identities are removed. The bounded row covers exact UTF-16 locations, framed repeatability, malformed/stale/out-of-document/surrogate-splitting validation, cancellation, and cross-kind filtering.

features.label: Typed parameters, results, function values, and static checking
features.notes: Current implementation status: interpreter and VM preserve exact annotated widths and callable signatures, while unannotated source still remains dynamic. This is a known Core Semantics 1 deviation (CS1-D04), not a Core 1 claim; Tasks 08, 09, 03, and 07 own its removal. Native C supports the parity-tested represented kinds and exact closure signatures; annotations for runtime kinds absent from the C ABI are source-spanned compile-time boundaries. WASM scalar-i64-v1 artifacts execute constants, arithmetic, unary operations, comparisons, booleans, null, cyclic and acyclic branch/join control flow, generated instruction accounting, and result transport inside wazero; aggregate/provider forms remain bounded payload-v1 compatibility paths. GPU planning runs the shared checker before producing artifacts. LSP typed-function support is stable for the shared-checker surface: typed diagnostics, source-backed generic type-parameter hover/definition/references/completion, typed member completion/hover/definition/references, UTF-16 positions, signature-help parameter labels and active-parameter selection, malformed/stale request rejection, deterministic concurrent responses, and cancellation without partial publication are covered by maintained unit and framed protocol fixtures.

features.label: Constants, immutable runtime bindings, and mutable locals
features.notes: Core Semantics 1 requires statically restricted `const`, eager immutable `let`, explicit Lazy<T>, and ordered `var` assignment. Tasks 01 and 11 implement eager `let`, same-scope redeclaration rejection, backend-neutral parity probes, and compiled explicit Lazy<T> thunks across interpreter, VM, and native C. Evaluation ordering remains a known deviation (CS1-D01); this row records implementation evidence, not an alternate semantic contract. Aggregate field/index mutation remains an explicit unsupported boundary. LSP binding analysis is stable for scalar declarations: hover exposes constant, immutable, and mutable binding contracts; assignment references preserve the target identity; assignments to `const` and `let` produce source-spanned diagnostics; framed output is deterministic and retains UTF-16, stale-version, malformed-request, and cancellation boundaries from the shared LSP request layer.

features.label: Types, numeric families, units, and exact values
features.notes: The interpreter and VM share the exact rational quantity catalog, alias values, inference, and codecs. Native C lowers the tested named-product construction/member/update subset and supported default-number globals directly; aliases, newtypes, dimensioned named quantities, and unproved numeric families remain explicit boundaries. LSP source-backed alias/newtype declarations, struct-field type annotations, typed function parameter/return references, and numeric-literal cursors now resolve deterministic definitions with exact UTF-16 ranges; malformed, stale, and cancelled requests remain strict protocol errors.

features.label: Structured errors, Result, Option, and try/catch
features.notes: Native C reports selected runtime failures, but it does not yet claim complete structured-error parity.

features.label: Native error, Result, Option constructors and OSR1 codec
features.notes: Native C directly lowers error, ok, err, some, none, encode, and decode. The bounded row covers owned constructor boxes, independent payload tracking, OSR1 O_ERROR/O_RESULT/O_OPTION tags, canonical round trips, malformed-record rejection, exact arity diagnostics, wrong-kind failures, no host capability, and no interpreter/dispatcher fallback. try/catch, unwrap, expect, or_else, to_option, to_result, and collect remain part of the broader partial errors/results/options row.

features.label: Imports, packages, exports, version selectors, and macros
features.notes: LSP module navigation is stable for explicit exports from standard-library, source-backed user, and verified repository modules, plus hygienic macro declarations and parameters. Shared symbol identities drive completion, hover, definition, and references; repository selectors use verified lock/provider state; virtual and unresolved modules remain explicit non-results. Maintained fixtures cover UTF-16 positions, stale and malformed requests, cancellation, deterministic framing, and workspace-boundary behavior. Native C only propagates a static, tested import subset; dynamic and general module behavior is not a native promise.

features.label: match and switch expressions
features.notes: Interpreter and VM support closed enums with zero- and payload-case constructors, explicit unique string/fixed-width-integer backed declarations, named-product/struct patterns with nominal type and recursive named-field matching, nested qualified patterns, guards, final default arms, grouped alternatives with stable bindings, relational, type-binding, conjunction, and negation patterns, plus static exhaustiveness for resolvable enum subjects. Native C supports tagged enum and named-product construction/matching, recursive equality and rendering, truthiness, nested enum/list/function/product payloads, literals, every C-ABI type pattern, relational, conjunction, negation, repeated bindings, final defaults, compatible grouped alternatives, guards, and backed declaration metadata through generated CFG. LSP pattern navigation is stable for enum and struct patterns: source-backed type and field definitions, nested binding references, exact UTF-16 ranges, deterministic framed responses, stale/malformed request rejection, and unsupported-field diagnostics are covered by maintained fixtures. Non-native runtime kinds remain explicit native compile-time boundaries rather than an interpreter fallback.

features.label: Tasks, cancellation, streams, and asynchronous I/O
features.notes: Native C has a cooperative deterministic subset for captured `spawn` thunks, repeated `await`, pending-task `cancel`, ordered `parallel`, and task failures crossing `try`/`catch`. Streams, host-backed asynchronous I/O, `race`, `select`, deadlines, and interruption of already-running host work remain unsupported.

features.label: Formatting, IR analysis, tracing, and editor protocol
features.notes: Analysis tools operate on source/IR. The CLI has an opt-in versioned JSON diagnostic envelope with stable stream separation and exit categories. Native cache, lock, and GPU JSON formats are versioned and validated. The optimizer emits ordered text or versioned JSON reports and names unavailable proof-dependent passes explicitly. LSP now has deterministic protocol evidence for every advertised request capability, incremental UTF-16 document updates, typed-member and standard-library completion/hover/definition/references, semantic tokens, inlay/folding/selection ranges, call/type hierarchy, code actions, formatting, pull diagnostics, cancellable colocated-test code lenses, and versioned workspace fixtures.

features.label: LSP executable test results
features.notes: The osiris/testResults request executes shared language-test discovery against open-document overlays and returns JSON-safe per-test status, outputs, assertions, logs, source locations, structured error text, and runtime duration. Interpreter and VM execution are covered by the language-test runner; Native C remains partial because the endpoint can only claim the currently supported generated-C test subset. Semantic fixture comparison ignores durationNS because it is a runtime measurement.

features.label: std/text
features.notes: Native C directly executes every exported std/text member: trim, trim_space, trim_left, trim_right, lower, upper, contains, contains_any, has_prefix, has_suffix, slug, cat, fields, join, compare, equal_fold, count, index, last_index, index_any, last_index_any, cut, cut_prefix, cut_suffix, trim_prefix, trim_suffix, replace, replace_n, split, split_after, split_n, split_after_n, chunks, and repeat. UTF-8 inputs and result sizes are bounded, owned strings/lists/options never retain caller storage, malformed and wrong-kind inputs return structured errors, and no host capability or interpreter fallback is used. LSP std/text export navigation is stable across the complete runtime module inventory: completion derives every exported member from the runtime module, while hover, definition, references, UTF-16, stale/malformed validation, cancellation, and deterministic framing are covered by maintained fixtures.

features.label: std/math scalar, complex, and constructor functions
features.notes: Interpreter and VM share the expanded floating decomposition, classification, angle, exact-integer, fixed-width bit, and principal-complex implementation. The new operations retain numeric width/style, use structured domain and representation errors, and have exact zero/overflow contracts. Native support remains restricted to explicitly lowered, parity-tested static math members. Newly added operations and complex transcendental forms reject at native compile time until Go/C last-bit, special-value, and branch-cut parity is proven. Existing inverse trigonometry, real hyperbolic functions, gamma, and log-gamma lower only for proven f32 scalar inputs; f64 forms remain rejected. Two-argument base log and pow/expt keep their documented narrow f32 native gates. LSP std/math export navigation is stable across the complete runtime module inventory, with deterministic completion, checked virtual identities, and the shared UTF-16, stale, malformed, and cancellation request boundary.

features.label: std/math.divmod fixed-width unsigned arithmetic
features.notes: Native C directly lowers the bounded fixed-width unsigned form. Two O_UINT operands with explicit widths from 1 through 64 bits return an owned [quotient, remainder] list using the wider width; zero divisors, signed values, unsupported numeric families, and wrong arity produce structured failures. The generated code uses ostd_math_divmod without indirect dispatch, evaluator fallback, or host capability. The broader std/math scalar row remains partial for its other numeric families.

features.label: std/math floating remainder and fused multiply-add
features.notes: Native C directly lowers fmod, remainder, and fma for matching-width default floating, f32, and f64 scalars. Inputs are borrowed and allocation-free; fmod and remainder reject zero divisors with structured invalid-argument errors, while fma preserves one fused rounding step. Complex, integer, mixed-width, dynamic, host-capability, and indirect-dispatch forms remain explicit compile boundaries.

features.label: std/math fixed-width unsigned bit operations
features.notes: Native C directly executes count_ones, count_zeros, leading_zeros, trailing_zeros, bit_width, bit_floor, bit_ceil, has_single_bit, and byte_swap for explicit fixed-width unsigned values. Results preserve the declared width where applicable; zero behavior, ceiling overflow, non-byte-aligned swaps, wrong kinds, and wrong arity have structured contracts. Helpers are allocation-free, do not call the std/math dispatcher, and require no host capability. The broader std/math scalar row remains partial for other numeric families.

features.label: std/math fixed-width unsigned gcd and lcm
features.notes: Native C directly lowers gcd and lcm for explicit fixed-width unsigned operands. Results use the wider input width; zero inputs, mixed widths, overflow checks, zero-divisor-free gcd behavior, direct helper selection, ownership, and capability boundaries are covered. Signed, arbitrary-precision, and floating forms remain outside this bounded row.

features.label: std/math numeric extrema and clamp
features.notes: Native C directly lowers the documented numeric subset of min, max, and clamp through owned scalar values without module dispatch or host capability. Variadic non-empty extrema, mixed numeric inputs, f32/f64 width preservation, and clamp bounds are covered; unsupported numeric families remain explicit failures under the broader std/math row.

features.label: Array constructors
features.notes: Native coverage is limited to tested static math constructors and contiguous tensor forms.

features.label: Range generators
features.notes: Native coverage is limited to tested static range generators and contiguous tensor forms.

features.label: Tensor operations
features.notes: Native C covers a growing, parity-tested tensor kernel set; unsupported tensor operations are rejected at compile time.

features.label: Matrix operations
features.notes: Native C supports a tested subset of matrix construction and operations; unsupported matrices and kernels remain compile-time boundaries.

features.label: Shape operations
features.notes: Shape inference and validation are fully supported in the interpreter and VM; native support is limited to shapes proven by its tested lowering paths.

features.label: Linear algebra
features.notes: Native C linear algebra is stable for the documented bounded kernel and configured numerical-provider ABI surface. Portable generated-C fixtures execute `eig`, `eigh`, and `svd` through explicit ABI-versioned providers, return owned tensor/list aggregates, reject missing or incompatible providers with structured compile/runtime errors, and preserve interpreter/VM/native output parity. The backend does not claim a bundled general-purpose solver: production provider availability and alternate-platform adapters remain explicit deployment requirements.

features.label: Reductions and statistics
features.notes: Native reduction coverage is limited to parity-tested scalar and contiguous tensor kernels.

features.label: I/O helpers
features.notes: The interpreter and VM share explicit file, directory, metadata, bounded-copy/read, deterministic listing, seekable-stream, lifecycle, cancellation, and structured-error contracts. Native C executes the bounded POSIX file, stream, mutation, metadata, and rooted-resource subset through owned descriptors, including non-root links, and emits a guarded Windows HANDLE adapter for the corresponding resources. Flag-derived write grants, callback-backed raw handles, and asynchronous transfer remain explicit boundaries.

features.label: Data helpers and codecs
features.notes: Native C supports the versioned `OSR1` codec for its parity-tested scalar, string, list, UTC datetime, duration, and complex families, including cross-direction and malformed-input checks. Other codec tags and data-pipeline helpers remain unsupported.

features.label: Native OSR1 scalar and structured-value codecs
features.notes: Native C directly encodes and decodes the bounded OSR1 scalar, string, list, UTC datetime, duration, complex, Error, Result, and Option tree. Cross-direction parity, canonical tags, malformed framing/version/presence/truncation rejection, recursive depth/size bounds, tracked decoded copies, independently owned payload boxes, exact constructor arity, wrong-kind failures, and no host capability or interpreter fallback are maintained. Other codec tags and data-pipeline helpers remain outside this row and the aggregate data-helpers row remains partial.

features.label: std/crypto
features.notes: Native C directly executes every exported `std/crypto` member: version and bound constants, SHA algorithm constants, seeded `random`, `hash`, `mix`, `noise`, digest text/bytes, HMAC, constant-time comparison, hexadecimal and standard/URL-safe Base64 codecs, deterministic key derivation, seeded byte generation, deterministic tokens, UUID v5, and algorithm queries. Each member has bounded validation, owned outputs, deterministic structured errors, no host capability requirement, and interpreter/VM/generated-executable evidence. LSP std/crypto export navigation is stable across the complete runtime module inventory with deterministic completion and the shared virtual-identity, UTF-16, stale, malformed, and cancellation contract.

features.label: std/signal
features.notes: Native C directly executes every exported std/signal member: version, max_samples, max_transform_samples, pi, all five windows, convolve, correlate, filter_fir, resample, mean, variance, energy, rms, normalize, fft, and ifft. Numeric inputs are bounded and copied into temporary staging storage; tensor results are newly owned, scalar results are returned by value, deterministic constants use direct lowering, and no host capability is required. LSP std/signal export navigation is stable across the complete runtime module inventory with deterministic completion and the shared virtual-identity, UTF-16, stale, malformed, and cancellation contract.

features.label: std/list
features.notes: Native C directly executes every exported `std/list` member: `range`, `len`, `take`, `sum`, `product`, `reverse`, `at`, `index_of`, `last_index_of`, `contains`, `count`, `sort`, `unique`, `partition`, `slice`, `chunks`, `windows`, `zip`, `concat`, `repeat`, `empty`, `all`, `any`, `none`, `enumerate`, and `flatten`. Each member has bounded argument validation, owned result construction, deterministic errors, no host capability requirement, and interpreter/VM/generated-executable differential evidence. LSP std/list export navigation is stable across the complete runtime module inventory with deterministic completion and the shared virtual-identity, UTF-16, stale, malformed, and cancellation contract.

features.label: std/time durations, datetimes, and locations
features.notes: Native C supports the tested UTC-only slice: `date`, `add_date`, `add`, `sub`, `parse_duration`, `duration_string`, `format`, `round`, `truncate`, `compare`, `equal`, `before`, `after`, `year`, `month`, `day`, `weekday`, `year_day`, `zone`, `utc_location`, and `rfc3339`, with no clock or timezone-database dependency. IANA/fixed locations, `now`, parsing, timers, and all unlisted members remain unsupported; the matrix status remains partial. LSP std/time export navigation is stable across the complete runtime module inventory with deterministic completion and the shared virtual-identity, UTF-16, stale, malformed, and cancellation contract.

features.label: std/time UTC conversion and zone projection
features.notes: Native C directly executes time.utc(datetime) and time.zone(datetime) for the current UTC-only datetime ABI. UTC conversion preserves the instant and normalized nanosecond by value; zone returns a newly owned ["UTC", 0i64] projection. Wrong kinds and arity remain structured failures, and neither operation reads a clock, loads timezone data, retains input storage, allocates host resources, or defines a capability. IANA/fixed-location behavior remains outside this bounded row and the aggregate std/time row remains partial.

features.label: Native interop and build flow
features.notes: Osiris can lower a tested subset through C and invoke the system C compiler. The FFI boundary validates capability-gated, digest-pinned manifests and has generated-C parity for declared scalar, float, string, constant, immutable-buffer, and mutable-buffer calls. Hosted and VM additionally cover fixed-layout records, opaque handles, and scoped synchronous callbacks; unsupported ABI shapes are rejected rather than coerced.

features.label: Lexical scope-bound cleanup
features.notes: `defer { ... }` captures the registration-time lexical environment and executes exactly once in LIFO order across normal, return, break, continue, propagated failure, cancellation, and task exits in the interpreter and VM. `close` preserves stream/socket APIs and dispatches zero-argument user resource methods; built-in handles are idempotent. Native C emits explicit cleanup thunks on every supported normal and early edge, including owned POSIX file, process, socket, TLS/HTTP, and watch resources; unsupported platform adapters remain explicit boundaries.

features.label: Native C synchronous scope-bound cleanup
features.notes: Native C emits owned cleanup thunks for synchronous scope exit, normal function return, loop control-flow edges, captured lexical values, and optimizer-preserved IR. The bounded row proves deterministic registration and execution without losing body results or retaining stale thunk state. Asynchronous cancellation, task termination, and the complete cross-platform host-resource close protocol remain in the broader partial scope-bound-cleanup row.

features.label: LSP std/net export inventory and navigation
features.notes: LSP completion derives every exported std/net member from the live runtime module, including capability-gated networking operations, without opening sockets or requiring host capability. The generic source-backed module path preserves deterministic ordering, virtual identity, UTF-16 conversion, stale/malformed validation, and cancellation; this row does not claim Native C network execution.

features.label: std/net TCP, UDP, DNS, TLS, and HTTP/1.1
features.notes: Hosted Go support is bounded and context-aware: UDP preserves peer/truncation metadata, DNS results are sorted and deduplicated, TLS verifies explicit roots and hostnames with TLS 1.2 minimum and HTTP/1.1 ALPN, and HTTP/1.1 enforces header, redirect, streaming, and body limits. Native C executes POSIX TCP/UDP/DNS, plain HTTP, and provider-backed verified TLS through owned resources. Native HTTP also implements bounded redirects and generated closure handlers; non-POSIX providers remain explicit platform boundaries.

features.label: Native std/os environment and identity
features.notes: Native C directly executes the bounded POSIX/macOS std/os environment and identity surface: missing getenv, sorted env_names/environ snapshots, explicitly capability-gated setenv mutation, path-separator checks, hostname, process IDs, and page size. Generated executables match the reference runtime under explicit os.environment, os.environment_mutate, and os.system_identity grants; capability normalization and missing-grant diagnostics are tested. Windows/Linux behavior and the broader filesystem/process/watch aggregate remain outside this row.

features.label: LSP std/os export inventory and navigation
features.notes: LSP completion derives every exported std/os member from the live runtime module, including filesystem, environment, process, identity, signal, and watch operations, without touching the host. The generic module path preserves deterministic ordering, virtual identity, UTF-16 conversion, stale/malformed validation, and cancellation; this row does not claim Native C host execution.

features.label: Native POSIX filesystem and rooted resources
features.notes: Native C directly executes the maintained POSIX/macOS filesystem and rooted-resource subset through owned descriptors and directory roots: bounded file I/O, metadata, mutation, root filesystem bridging, ownership/timestamp methods, and symlink-safe no-escape resolution. Capability gates, ownership, cleanup, deterministic errors, and generated executable parity are covered. Windows HANDLE adapters, Linux evidence, and unlisted filesystem operations remain outside this bounded row and the aggregate std/os row remains partial.

features.label: Native POSIX process handles and lifecycle
features.notes: Native C directly executes the maintained POSIX process-handle surface with owned spawn, wait, signal/kill, release, process streams, inherited and replacement environment overlays, process-group cancellation, timeout escalation, descendant cleanup, and reaping. Capability gates, cancellation ownership, cleanup, and interpreter/VM/generated-executable evidence are covered. Windows HANDLE adapters, Linux differential evidence, and unlisted process semantics remain outside this bounded row and the aggregate std/os row remains partial.

features.label: Native POSIX standard streams, signals, and watches
features.notes: Native C directly executes the maintained POSIX standard-stream, raw-handle, signal-subscription, and bounded watch snapshot resources with explicit capability checks and owned lifecycle cleanup. Windows HANDLE adapters, Linux evidence, callback closure breadth, and unlisted watch semantics remain outside this bounded row and the aggregate std/os row remains partial.

features.label: std/os filesystem, identity, process, environment, signals, and watching
features.notes: Hosted Go support exposes the expanded capability-gated std/os surface: bounded owned file handles, deterministic fake filesystem/environment/identity/clock/platform/process providers, metadata and path mutation, rooted access with derived-handle invalidation, shell-free child processes with cancellation, bounded signals, and portable snapshot watching. Native C executes the POSIX resource subset: file/stream/process/root/metadata handles, path mutation, deterministic environment overlays, process-group cleanup, producer-aware generic resource capabilities, standard streams, raw handles, bounded signals, and snapshot watch streams, with no shell fallback. Generated C also emits a guarded Windows HANDLE/Winsock adapter for the same resource families. Linux generated-C differential and AddressSanitizer evidence are recorded by deferred native host; Windows execution evidence and callback-backed raw-handle semantics remain explicit platform/ABI boundaries.
